title: UPDATE: OpenAI Scales ChatGPT Ad Tools for 1.2 Billion Weekly Users
summary:
The AI developer is launching conversion-tracking software to measure the effectiveness of ads appearing in its chatbot. OpenAI is integrating a suite of attribution and brand-safety tools from partners including LiveRamp, Tealium, Hightouch, AppsFlyer, Adjust and Branch to quantify ROI on a platform that now reaches 1.2 billion people weekly. Early campaign data shows WeightWatchers achieved a cost per acquisition 15.3% below its paid-search benchmark, while 93% of visitors to Portland Leather from these ads were new users.

These measurement tools support new display ads that will appear during image generation in ChatGPT starting later this month in the US. The ads will be clearly labeled and remain separate from the generated content to ensure they do not interfere with the chatbot's responses. OpenAI is also partnering with DoubleVerify and Integral Ad Science to perform brand-suitability testing for the initial group of advertisers.

🚨BREAKING: OpenAI will begin testing visual ads during image generation in ChatGPT later this month, initially in the US, as ChatGPT now reaches 1.2 billion people every week. The ads will remain separate from the image being created.

OpenAI also says early advertiser results have been strong: WeightWatchers’ CPA on ChatGPT Ads was 15.3% below its paid-search benchmark, 67% of Dose’s incremental purchases came from net-new customers, and 93% of Portland Leather’s ChatGPT Ads visitors were new.

OpenAI introduces visual ads to ChatGPT

"This new, visual ad unit in ChatGPT is a display ad, and it’s rendered in a context that likely includes little to no commercial intent. This ties directly to the point I make in The privileged position of chatbot advertising, which is that chatbot advertising enjoys an either/or benefit. Either a conversation has a commercial locus, in which case ads can be anchored to it, or it doesn’t, in which case ads can be anchored to the conversion data that advertisers emit to platforms through their CAPI implementations or pixels."
